newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco sees nickel demand topping output.
newsitem.headline: Inco sees nickel demand topping output.

text.p: Inco Ltd Chief Executive Michael Sopko said on Wednesday that nickel demand in 1997 would likely reach a new high and the Canadian nickel producer anticipated demand would exceed production for the year.
"To capitalize on strong demand, we plan to operate at capacity, producing about 430 million pounds of nickel in 1997," Sopko said in a prepared speech to the annual meeting.
Sopko said that looking beyond 1997, "our best estimate at this time is that nickel demand will exceed production in both 1998 and 1999."
Inco on Tuesday reported that first-quarter net earnings fell to US$58 million or US$0.27 a share from year earlier US$63 million or US$0.49 a share.
"Our first-quarter results...are encouraging, but we are hopeful we can and will do better over the balance of the year," Sopko said in his speech.
